head: cloud/tp2-rank1-request-errors
title: fix(tp2): keep rank 1 alive when one request's snapshot or batched token fails
body:
> AI disclosure: I am not a software developer. Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) developed and tested this patch; an independent Claude Fable 5.1 review approved it before submission; this is not a claim of human developer review. Claude Code cloud session, CPU only, no GPU testing.

Test scope: CPU build/tests only, on an x86-64 cloud VM with no GPU and no RDMA (`cmake --preset cpu-test`, GCC 13, `GUFO_ENABLE_TP2_RDMA` off, since that option needs HIP), on this branch rebased onto `rdma` at 97d3b3d. Each of the two new `tp_executor_test` cases fails on 97d3b3d without its fix (`FAIL: drop of an uncaptured snapshot ID`; `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'` / `invalid token accepted by JSON constraint`) and passes with it. `ctest --preset cpu-test -L tp2` passed 4/4. `cmake --build --preset pr` passed 63/63. `nix shell --inputs-from . nixpkgs#clang-tools -c python3 tools/ci/check-format.py` (the pinned clang-tools) passes: `PASS: Checked 613 C++ files`. Built in a cloud session (CPU only); Strix Halo validation pending.

Two places where one request's failure on rank 1 ends the rank-1 worker, and with it the pair, instead of failing that request. Both are in `tp_executor.cpp`, and each commit has its own test.

## 1. A drop of a capture ID rank 1 refused or never received

When a snapshot capture fails, rank 0's `TpMirroredRunner::Capture` catches the error and calls `Drop(id)`, which sends `kDrop` for that ID outside any request. Rank 1 only records the ID (`last_snapshot_id_`) after its divergence check. So when rank 1 refuses the capture (it already noted a failure for this request, or the ranks' call counts or digests differ), it acknowledges with an error but never records the ID. The following `kDrop` then hits `DropSnapshot`'s `id > last_snapshot_id_` check and throws `unknown snapshot drop ID`. `Execute` returns false, and the rank-1 worker loop in `inference_backend.cpp` exits, which takes down the pair instead of only skipping one snapshot. The comment in `ExecuteCall` says a failed capture "only means no snapshot", and rank 0 drops the ID afterwards; rank 1 did not match that for refusals that happen before the ID is recorded.

The same drop also arrives when `Capture` fails on rank 0 before the `kSnapshot` instruction is sent at all, so rank 1 never saw that ID.

Fix:

- `ExecuteCall` (`kSnapshot`): record the ID right after the reused-ID check, before the divergence check, so a refused capture still retires its ID.
- `DropSnapshot`: accept a drop of an ID above `last_snapshot_id_` (rank 0 allocated it, but the capture never reached rank 1) and retire it, so a later `kSnapshot` that reuses it is still refused. ID 0 is still an error.

Test: a request whose `kSnapshot` names the wrong call count (rank 1 refuses it), then idle drops of ID 1 (refused) and ID 2 (never sent). Both drops must leave the worker running and keep no snapshot. Without the fix the test fails with `FAIL: drop of an uncaptured snapshot ID`.

## 2. A constraint that refuses a token in a batched advance or decode

In `ExecuteCall`, `request.sampler.Accept(token)` runs inside the call's `try`, so a constrained request whose rebuilt constraint refuses rank 0's token is noted as failed (`DigestTpFailure` + `Note`) and rank 0 gets that verdict. `ExecuteBatch` runs the same `Accept`, plus the digest and checkpoint update, outside any `try`. When the constraint refuses the token there, `ConstraintVocabulary` throws `invalid token accepted by JSON constraint`, the exception leaves `Execute`, and the rank-1 worker ends. The other batch members' digests are not recorded either.

Rank 1's constraint only refuses a token rank 0 accepted once rank 1's state for that request has already gone wrong (for example its own selections differed, or an earlier call failed and skipped `Accept`). Those cases are meant to fail that one request with a verdict, as they do in `ExecuteCall`.

Fix: wrap each member's `Accept` and digest update in `ExecuteBatch` in a `try`. On an exception the member gets `DigestTpFailure` and a `rank 1 batched advance failed: ...` (or `batched decode`) note, like the serial path, and the loop goes on to the next member.

Test: `ToyRunner` gains a `constraint` option that offers a constraint vocabulary (no toy piece is JSON, so a `json_object` constraint refuses every token). A constrained and an unconstrained request share a `kAdvanceBatch`. `Execute` must return true, the constrained request's verdict must name `batched advance failed`, and the other request must stay open. Without the fix the test binary aborts with `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'` / `invalid token accepted by JSON constraint`.

## Not changed

`run_worker` in `inference_backend.cpp` still ends on any exception from `Execute`; this PR only stops these two request-level failures from reaching it.

review.summary: Both fixes are correct and consistent with rank 0's protocol ordering (call_mutex_ serialises ID allocation, send and drop), the tests reproduce the failures, every claim in the body is backed by the evidence and by an independent re-run of the test binary, the pr CTest log and the pinned clang-format, the disclosure line is correct and first, the title follows RELEASING.md, and there is no sensitive or off-topic content.
